content.text: Take w/ meals and a glass of H2O; ⍉ on an empty stomach (potential for gastric irritate).

CI: hyperkalemia (further ↑ serum K can prod ♡ arrest). CI: any struct, pathological, or pharm cause for arrest or delay in tablet passage thru the GI tract. In pts w/ impaired K excretion, potassium salts can prod hyperkalemia and ♡ arrest; potentially fatal hyperkalemia can develop rapidly and be aSx. ⍉ tx hypokalemia w/ concomitant potassium salts and a potassium-sparing diuretic (ex, spironolactone, triamterene, or amiloride): severe hyperkalemia. Closely monitor K w/ concomitant RAAS therapy (ACEis, ARBs, spironolactone, eplerenone, or aliskiren). Closely monitor K w/ concomitant NSAID therapy. D/c STAT and consider ulceration, obstruct, or perf if severe vomiting, abd pain, distention, or GI bleed occurs. Careful monitoring of serum K and appropriate dosage adj required in chronic renal dz or any condition impairing K excretion. OD: hyperkalemia = USU aSx and may be manifested only by an ↑ serum K (6.5 to 8 mEq/L) and ECG chgs (peaking T-waves, loss of P-waves, S-T depression, QT prolongation). OD tx: IV calcium gluconate if the pt = @ ⍉risk or ↓risk of developing digitalis toxicity.
